nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement:
First, observe that assumptions (a) and (b) and the triangle inequality for $e$ imply, for all $s,t\in T$, $s\le t$, and $X,Y\in\mbox{c}(M)$,  egin{equation} e(F(s,X),F(t,Y))\le\varphi(t)-\varphi(s)+\mu d_H(X,Y). \end{equation} We set $X_0(t)\!:=\!X_0$ and $F_0(t)\!:=\!F(t,X_0)$ for $t\in T$. We have \mbox{$F_0:T	o\mbox{c}(M)$}, and assumption (a) and Lemma~ef{l:char} imply $iV(F_0,T)\le
V(\varphi,T)<+\infty$. By Theorem~ef{t:BV}(a), there is $X_1\equiv\Gamma:T=T_{[t_0,+\infty)}	o\mbox{c}(M)$ such that $X_1(t)\subset F_0(t)$ for all $t\in T$, $d_H(X_0,X_1(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_0(t_0))$, and $
V(X_1,T)\leiV(F_0,T)\le
V(\varphi,T)$. In what follows we apply the standard iteration procedure. Setting $F_1(t):=F(t,X_1(t))$ for $t\in T$, we find $F_1:T	o\mbox{c}(M)$ and, by \eq{e:XY},  egin{equation*} e(F_1(s),F_1(t))\le\varphi(t)-\varphi(s)+\mu d_H(X_1(s),X_1(t))\quad  orall\,s,t\in T,\,\,s\le t. \end{equation*} Arguing with partitions of $T$, Lemma~ef{l:char} implies  egin{equation*} iV(F_1,T)\le
V(\varphi,T)+\mu
V(X_1,T)\le(1+\mu)
V(\varphi,T). \end{equation*} Applying Theorem~ef{t:BV} again, we obtain $X_2:T	o\mbox{c}(M)$ such that $X_2(t)\subset F_1(t)$ for all $t\in T$, $d_H(X_0,X_2(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_1(t_0))$, and  egin{equation*} 
V(X_2,T)\leiV(F_1,T)\le(1+\mu)
V(\varphi,T). \end{equation*} If $F_2(t)\!:=\!F(t,X_2(t))$, $t\in T$, then $F_2:T	o\mbox{c}(M)$ and, by \eq{e:XY},  egin{equation*} e(F_2(s),F_2(t))\le\varphi(t)-\varphi(s)+\mu d_H(X_2(s),X_2(t))\quad  orall\,s,t\in T,\,\,s\le t, \end{equation*} and so,  egin{equation*} iV(F_2,T)\le
V(\varphi,T)+\mu
V(X_2,T)\le(1+\mu+\mu^2)
V(\varphi,T). \end{equation*} Arguing by induction, we obtain the sequence $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ of multifunctions $X_n:T	o\mbox{c}(M)$ such that, given $n\in\Nb$,  egin{eqnarray} &X_n(t)\subset F_{n-1}(t)\!:=\!F(t,X_{n-1}(t))\subset K(t)\quad\mbox{for all $t\in T$,}& \[3pt] &d_H(X_0,X_n(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_{n-1}(t_0))\!=\!e igl(X_0,F(t_0,X_{n-1}(t_0)) igr), \,\,\mbox{and}& \ &\displaystyle
V(X_n,T)\le iggl(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\mu^i iggr)
V(\varphi,T) \le rac1{1-\mu}\,
V(\varphi,T).& \end{eqnarray} By \eq{e:Vft}, the sequence $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ is of uniformly bounded Jordan variation with respect to $d_H$, and so, condition (a) in Theorem~ef{t:B} is satisfied, and by \eq{e:Xnt}, the closure $\ov{\{X_n(t):n\in\Nb\}}$ in $\mbox{c}(M)$ is compact for every $t\in T$, and so, condition (b) in Theorem~ef{t:B} is fulfiled. By Theorem~ef{t:B}, a subsequence of $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$, again denoted by $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$, converges in $\mbox{c}(M)$ pointwise on $T$ to a multifunction $X:T	o\mbox{c}(M)$, i.e., $d_H(X_n(t),X(t))	o0$ as $n	o\infty$ for all $t\in T$. We are going to verify that $X$ satisfies assertions (i), (ii), and (iii). Assertion (i) is a consequence of \eq{e:Vft} and the lower semicontinuity \eq{e:Vsem} of~$
V$. In order to see that (ii) holds, we make use of the following inequality (cf. \cite[inequality~(11.7)]{Sovae}), which is valid for all $X,X',Y,Y'\in\mbox{c}(M)$:  egin{equation} |e(X,Y)-e(X',Y')|\le d_H(X,X')+d_H(Y,Y'). \end{equation} In fact, given $t\in T$, \eq{e:Xnt} implies $e igl(X_n(t),F(t,X_{n-1}(t)) igr)=0$, and so, taking into account \eq{e:Sog} and \eq{e:XY}, we get  egin{align*} e(X(t),F(t,X(t)))&\!=\! igl|e(X(t),F(t,X(t)))\!-\!e(X_n(t),F(t,X_{n-1}(t))) igr|\[2pt] &\!\le\! d_H(X(t),X_n(t))\!+\!d_H(F(t,X(t)),F(t,X_{n-1}(t)))\[2pt] &\!\le\! d_H(X(t),X_n(t))\!+\!\mu d_H(X(t),X_{n-1}(t))	o0 \,\,\,\,\mbox{as}\,\,\,n	o\infty. \end{align*} Thus, $e(X(t),F(t,X(t)))=0$, which implies (by properties of~$e$) assertion~(ii). To establish (iii), we note that (cf. \eq{e:Hot} and (iii))  egin{equation*} |d_H(X_0,X_n(t_0))-d_H(X_0,X(t_0))|\le d_H(X_n(t_0),X(t_0))	o0 \,\,\,\,\mbox{as}\,\,\,n	o\infty, \end{equation*} and, by virtue of \eq{e:Sog} and assumption (b),  egin{align*} &\qquad igl|e(X_0,F(t_0,X_{n-1}(t_0)))-e(X_0,F(t_0,X(t_0))) igr|\[2pt] \le&\,d_H(F(t_0,X_{n-1}(t_0)),F(t_0,X(t_0)))\le\mu d_H(X_{n-1}(t_0),X(t_0)) 	o0,\,\,n	o\infty. \end{align*} Passing to the limit as $n	o\infty$ in \eq{e:Hot}, we arrive at~(iii). Finally, suppose $X_0\!\subset\! F(t_0,X_0)$. Hence $X_0\!\subset\! F_0(t_0)$ and $e(X_0,F_0(t_0))\!=\!0$. From the above, $d_H(X_0,X_1(t_0))\!\le\! e(X_0,F_0(t_0))\!=\!0$, and so, $X_1(t_0)\!=\!X_0$. Since  egin{equation*} X_0\subset F_0(t_0)=F(t_0,X_0)=F(t_0,X_1(t_0))=F_1(t_0), \end{equation*} we find from $d_H(X_0,X_2(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_1(t_0))=0$ that $X_2(t_0)=X_0$. By induction, we deduce from \eq{e:Hot} that $X_n(t_0)=X_0$ for all $n\in\Nb$. Passing to the lmit as $n	o\infty$ in \eq{e:Hot}, we get $d_H(X_0,X(t_0))\le e(X_0,F(t_0,X_0))=0$, which yields $X(t_0)=X_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Successive-approximation (Picard) iteration $X_n\subset F(\cdot,X_{n-1})$ built with Theorem 1(a), geometric-series variation bound $\nV(\varphi,T)/(1-\mu)$, then compactness via Theorem B and passage to the limit.

nodes.name: Combined estimate from assumptions (a) and (b)
nodes.statement: First, observe that assumptions (a) and (b) and the triangle inequality for $e$ imply, for all $s,t\in T$, $s\le t$, and $X,Y\in\mbox{c}(M)$, \begin{equation} e(F(s,X),F(t,Y))\le\varphi(t)-\varphi(s)+\mu d_H(X,Y). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality for $e$ gives $e(F(s,X),F(t,Y))\le\varphi(t)-\varphi(s)+\mu d_H(X,Y)$.

nodes.name: Base of the iteration: construct $X_1$ by Theorem 1(a)
nodes.statement:
We set $X_0(t)\!:=\!X_0$ and $F_0(t)\!:=\!F(t,X_0)$ for $t\in T$. We have \mbox{$F_0:T	o\mbox{c}(M)$}, and assumption (a) and Lemma~ef{l:char} imply $iV(F_0,T)\le
V(\varphi,T)<+\infty$. By Theorem~ef{t:BV}(a), there is $X_1\equiv\Gamma:T=T_{[t_0,+\infty)}	o\mbox{c}(M)$ such that $X_1(t)\subset F_0(t)$ for all $t\in T$, $d_H(X_0,X_1(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_0(t_0))$, and $
V(X_1,T)\leiV(F_0,T)\le
V(\varphi,T)$.
nodes.statement_short: With $F_0=F(\cdot,X_0)$, Lemma 1 bounds $\riV(F_0,T)$ and Theorem 1(a) yields $X_1$.

nodes.name: Iteration step: construct $X_2$ and bound $\riV(F_2,T)$
nodes.statement:
In what follows we apply the standard iteration procedure. Setting $F_1(t):=F(t,X_1(t))$ for $t\in T$, we find $F_1:T	o\mbox{c}(M)$ and, by \eq{e:XY},  egin{equation*} e(F_1(s),F_1(t))\le\varphi(t)-\varphi(s)+\mu d_H(X_1(s),X_1(t))\quad  orall\,s,t\in T,\,\,s\le t. \end{equation*} Arguing with partitions of $T$, Lemma~ef{l:char} implies  egin{equation*} iV(F_1,T)\le
V(\varphi,T)+\mu
V(X_1,T)\le(1+\mu)
V(\varphi,T). \end{equation*} Applying Theorem~ef{t:BV} again, we obtain $X_2:T	o\mbox{c}(M)$ such that $X_2(t)\subset F_1(t)$ for all $t\in T$, $d_H(X_0,X_2(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_1(t_0))$, and  egin{equation*} 
V(X_2,T)\leiV(F_1,T)\le(1+\mu)
V(\varphi,T). \end{equation*} If $F_2(t)\!:=\!F(t,X_2(t))$, $t\in T$, then $F_2:T	o\mbox{c}(M)$ and, by \eq{e:XY},  egin{equation*} e(F_2(s),F_2(t))\le\varphi(t)-\varphi(s)+\mu d_H(X_2(s),X_2(t))\quad  orall\,s,t\in T,\,\,s\le t, \end{equation*} and so,  egin{equation*} iV(F_2,T)\le
V(\varphi,T)+\mu
V(X_2,T)\le(1+\mu+\mu^2)
V(\varphi,T). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Repeat with $F_1=F(\cdot,X_1)$ to obtain $X_2$ and the partial geometric bounds $(1+\mu)$, $(1+\mu+\mu^2)$.

nodes.name: Induction and extraction of a pointwise limit via Theorem B
nodes.statement:
Arguing by induction, we obtain the sequence $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ of multifunctions $X_n:T	o\mbox{c}(M)$ such that, given $n\in\Nb$,  egin{eqnarray} &X_n(t)\subset F_{n-1}(t)\!:=\!F(t,X_{n-1}(t))\subset K(t)\quad\mbox{for all $t\in T$,}& \[3pt] &d_H(X_0,X_n(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_{n-1}(t_0))\!=\!e igl(X_0,F(t_0,X_{n-1}(t_0)) igr), \,\,\mbox{and}& \ &\displaystyle
V(X_n,T)\le iggl(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\mu^i iggr)
V(\varphi,T) \le rac1{1-\mu}\,
V(\varphi,T).& \end{eqnarray} By \eq{e:Vft}, the sequence $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ is of uniformly bounded Jordan variation with respect to $d_H$, and so, condition (a) in Theorem~ef{t:B} is satisfied, and by \eq{e:Xnt}, the closure $\ov{\{X_n(t):n\in\Nb\}}$ in $\mbox{c}(M)$ is compact for every $t\in T$, and so, condition (b) in Theorem~ef{t:B} is fulfiled. By Theorem~ef{t:B}, a subsequence of $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$, again denoted by $\{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$, converges in $\mbox{c}(M)$ pointwise on $T$ to a multifunction $X:T	o\mbox{c}(M)$, i.e., $d_H(X_n(t),X(t))	o0$ as $n	o\infty$ for all $t\in T$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction gives a sequence with uniformly bounded variation $\nV(\varphi,T)/(1-\mu)$ and values in $K(t)$; Theorem B extracts a pointwise limit $X$.

nodes.name: Verification of assertions (i) and (ii)
nodes.statement: We are going to verify that $X$ satisfies assertions (i), (ii), and (iii). Assertion (i) is a consequence of \eq{e:Vft} and the lower semicontinuity \eq{e:Vsem} of~$\nV$. In order to see that (ii) holds, we make use of the following inequality (cf. \cite[inequality~(11.7)]{Sovae}), which is valid for all $X,X',Y,Y'\in\mbox{c}(M)$: \begin{equation} |e(X,Y)-e(X',Y')|\le d_H(X,X')+d_H(Y,Y'). \end{equation} In fact, given $t\in T$, \eq{e:Xnt} implies $e\bigl(X_n(t),F(t,X_{n-1}(t))\bigr)=0$, and so, taking into account \eq{e:Sog} and \eq{e:XY}, we get \begin{align*} e(X(t),F(t,X(t)))&\!=\!\bigl|e(X(t),F(t,X(t)))\!-\!e(X_n(t),F(t,X_{n-1}(t)))\bigr|\\[2pt] &\!\le\! d_H(X(t),X_n(t))\!+\!d_H(F(t,X(t)),F(t,X_{n-1}(t)))\\[2pt] &\!\le\! d_H(X(t),X_n(t))\!+\!\mu d_H(X(t),X_{n-1}(t))\to0 \,\,\,\,\mbox{as}\,\,\,n\to\infty. \end{align*} Thus, $e(X(t),F(t,X(t)))=0$, which implies (by properties of~$e$) assertion~(ii).
nodes.statement_short: (i) from lower semicontinuity of $\nV$; (ii) from $e(X(t),F(t,X(t)))=0$ via the stability inequality for $e$.

nodes.name: Verification of assertion (iii)
nodes.statement: To establish (iii), we note that (cf. \eq{e:Hot} and (iii)) \begin{equation*} |d_H(X_0,X_n(t_0))-d_H(X_0,X(t_0))|\le d_H(X_n(t_0),X(t_0))\to0 \,\,\,\,\mbox{as}\,\,\,n\to\infty, \end{equation*} and, by virtue of \eq{e:Sog} and assumption (b), \begin{align*} &\qquad\bigl|e(X_0,F(t_0,X_{n-1}(t_0)))-e(X_0,F(t_0,X(t_0)))\bigr|\\[2pt] \le&\,d_H(F(t_0,X_{n-1}(t_0)),F(t_0,X(t_0)))\le\mu d_H(X_{n-1}(t_0),X(t_0)) \to0,\,\,n\to\infty. \end{align*} Passing to the limit as $n\to\infty$ in \eq{e:Hot}, we arrive at~(iii).
nodes.statement_short: Both sides of the initial-value estimate are continuous along the sequence, so pass to the limit.

nodes.name: The case $X_0\subset F(t_0,X_0)$: exact initial value
nodes.statement: Finally, suppose $X_0\!\subset\! F(t_0,X_0)$. Hence $X_0\!\subset\! F_0(t_0)$ and $e(X_0,F_0(t_0))\!=\!0$. From the above, $d_H(X_0,X_1(t_0))\!\le\! e(X_0,F_0(t_0))\!=\!0$, and so, $X_1(t_0)\!=\!X_0$. Since \begin{equation*} X_0\subset F_0(t_0)=F(t_0,X_0)=F(t_0,X_1(t_0))=F_1(t_0), \end{equation*} we find from $d_H(X_0,X_2(t_0))\le e(X_0,F_1(t_0))=0$ that $X_2(t_0)=X_0$. By induction, we deduce from \eq{e:Hot} that $X_n(t_0)=X_0$ for all $n\in\Nb$. Passing to the lmit as $n\to\infty$ in \eq{e:Hot}, we get $d_H(X_0,X(t_0))\le e(X_0,F(t_0,X_0))=0$, which yields $X(t_0)=X_0$.
nodes.statement_short: By induction $X_n(t_0)=X_0$ for all $n$, hence $X(t_0)=X_0$ in the limit.

nodes.name: Stability of the excess under perturbation of both arguments
nodes.statement: we make use of the following inequality (cf. \cite[inequality~(11.7)]{Sovae}), which is valid for all $X,X',Y,Y'\in\mbox{c}(M)$: \begin{equation} |e(X,Y)-e(X',Y')|\le d_H(X,X')+d_H(Y,Y'). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $|e(X,Y)-e(X',Y')|\le d_H(X,X')+d_H(Y,Y')$ for compact sets.
assumptions: which is valid for all $X,X',Y,Y'\in\mbox{c}(M)$

nodes.name: Degenerate cases of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: If $F(t,X)=F(t)$ is independent of $X\in\mbox{c}(M)$ (or $\mu=0$), Theorem~\ref{t:FuEm} gives back Theorem~\ref{t:BV}(a): we may set $\varphi=\ori{v}_{F}$ and~$K=F$. On the other hand, if $F(t,X)=F(X)$ is independent of $t\in T$ (or $\varphi\equiv0$), Theorem~\ref{t:FuEm} is a consequence of Banach's Contraction Theorem (in fact, $F:\mbox{c}(K)\to\mbox{c}(K)$ is a contraction on compact, hence complete, metric space $(\mbox{c}(K),d_H)$ with $K=K(t_0)$).
nodes.statement_short: $\mu=0$ recovers Theorem 1(a); $\varphi\equiv0$ reduces to Banach's contraction theorem on $(\mbox{c}(K),d_H)$.

nodes.name: Example 6 (the hypotheses of Theorem 2 are satisfiable: $F(t,X)=\varphi_0(t)X$)
nodes.statement: The purpose of this example is to show that assumptions of Theorem~\ref{t:FuEm} can be fulfiled. Let $M=\mathbb{B}$ be a Banach space with norm $|\cdot|$ and metric $d(x,y)=|x-y|$, $x,y\in M$, and $K\in\mbox{c}(M)$. Suppose $\varphi_0:T\to[0,+\infty)$ is nondecreasing and $\mu\!:=\!\sup_{t\in T}\varphi_0(t)<1$. Define $F:T\times\mbox{c}(M)\to\mbox{c}(M)$ by $F(t,X):=\varphi_0(t)X$ for $t\in T$ and $X\in\mbox{c}(M)$. We have \begin{equation*} e(F(s,X),F(t,X))\le\bigl(\varphi_0(t)-\varphi_0(s)\bigr)\max_{x\in X}|x|\quad \mbox{for all $s,t\in T$, $s\le t$,} \end{equation*} and so, condition (a) in Theorem~\ref{t:FuEm} is satisfied with $\varphi(t)\!:=\!\varphi_0(t)\max_{x\in K}|x|$, $t\in T$, for all $X\in\mbox{c}(K)$.
nodes.statement_short: Scaling a compact set by a nondecreasing $\varphi_0$ with $\sup\varphi_0<1$ satisfies conditions (a), (b), (c).

nodes.name: Example 7 (Cantor-type solutions of the functional inclusion)
nodes.statement: In Example~\ref{ex:6.1}, we set $\mathbb{B}:=\Rb$, $K:=[0,1]$, and $\varphi_0(t):=t$ for $t\in T:=[0,1/2]$ (hence $\mu=1/2$, $\varphi=\varphi_0$, and $\nV(\varphi,T)=1/2$). Define $F$ by \begin{equation*} F(t,X):=(tX)\cup(1-t+tX),\quad t\in T,\,\,X\in\mbox{c}(K). \end{equation*} For instance, if $X=[0,1]$, we have $F(0,X)=\{0,1\}$, $F(1/2,X)=[0,1]$, and if $0<t<1/2$, then $F(t,X)=[0,t]\cup[1-t,1]$, $F(t,[0,t])=[0,t^2]\cup[1-t,1-t+t^2]$, $F(t,[1-t,1])=[t-t^2,t]\cup[1-t^2,1]$, and so on. The iterative construction of the classical Cantor (ternary) set corresponds to $t=1/3$ (e.g., \cite[p.~20]{GK}). By Theorem~\ref{t:FuEm}, there is $X:[0,1/2]\to\mbox{c}([0,1])$ such that $\nV(X,[0,1/2])\!\le\!1$, $X(t)\subset(tX(t))\cup(1-t+tX(t))$ for all $t\in[0,1/2]$, and $X(0)=\{0,1\}$. For every $t\in(0,1/2)$, the compact set $X(t)\subset[0,1]$ is a Cantor-type perfect set.
nodes.statement_short: $F(t,X)=(tX)\cup(1-t+tX)$ on $[0,1/2]$ produces solutions $X(t)$ that are Cantor-type perfect sets, the classical ternary set at $t=1/3$.
